entries.title: Exodus 32:1
segments: Out of the mount;

Gods; idols, or an idol to represent God. 
 
  Wot; know. 
 
Into whatever engagements men enter to serve the Lord, if left to their own sinful inclinations they will soon break them, and plunge into wickedness, to their disgrace and ruin.

entries.title: Exodus 32:6
segments:
Play; engage in revelling and wantonness. 
 
Those forms of religion which gratify the pride, selfishness, and carnal inclinations of men, while they attract great numbers, instead of making them better, only make them worse and ripen them for divine judgments.

entries.title: Exodus 32:7
segments: Thy people, which thou broughtest; he says not, my people, whom I brought; but, thy people, which thou broughtest; as if he would disown Israel as his people.

entries.title: Exodus 32:9
segments: Stiff-necked; refusing to yield obedience to the commands of God.

entries.title: Exodus 32:10
segments: Let me alone; do not ask me to spare them.

entries.title: Exodus 32:11
segments: Moses in reply says, Thy people, which thou hast brought, and adds also that it was with a mighty hand; because he means to plead the covenant relation of God to Israel, and the wonders He has already wrought in their behalf, as a reason why He should spare them.  In this prayer the one appeal of Moses is to Jehovah's glory; and this is a prevailing plea.

entries.title: Exodus 32:12
segments: Repent of this evil; not destroy the people, but spare them.

entries.title: Exodus 32:14
segments: Prayer for sinners, offered from regard to the glory of God, has great influence with him, and is often the means of changing his conduct towards them; so that, instead of destroying them, he brings them to repentance, and bestows upon them precious and everlasting mercies.

entries.title: Exodus 32:15
segments: Tables of the testimony; those on which God had written the ten commandments.

entries.title: Exodus 32:19
segments: He--broke them; to show the people, in a significant manner, that they had broken the covenant into which they had solemnly entered,
, and deserved to be destroyed.

entries.title: Exodus 32:20
segments: The water; which flowed from the rock,
, and of which the people continued to drink.

entries.title: Exodus 32:24
segments: When good men connive at iniquity, and especially when they aid in promoting it, their guilt is exceedingly great, and the excuses which they make are both cowardly and foolish.  If such conduct does not bring destruction on themselves, it may on multitudes of others.

entries.title: Exodus 32:25
segments: Naked; stripped of their ornaments, and exposed.

entries.title: Exodus 32:27
segments: His brother--companion, and--neighbor; all who had been engaged in this idolatry.

entries.title: Exodus 32:29
segments:
Consecrate yourselves; devote yourselves to the Lord, in the execution of his will in punishing the transgressors. 
 
It is sometimes a duty to take away human life; and in doing it we may honor God, do good to men, and secure special divine favor.  When done at the command of God, or in obedience to his will, it is a proper and useful expression of his indignation against sin.

entries.title: Exodus 32:30
segments: Make an atonement; obtain mercy for them.

entries.title: Exodus 32:32
segments: Blot me--out of thy book; if thou destroy them let me die also, and not live to see thy dishonor and thy ruin.

entries.title: Exodus 32:34
segments:
Visit; that is, with evils. 
 
Respite or delay of punishment is not forgiveness; and persons may be spared for a time, and yet afterwards be destroyed.  The goodness of God in delaying punishment, should lead all to repentance.  If it does not, it will in the end aggravate their ruin.
